declared_in: reports/decision.md, section "Gradient boosting comparison: declared Nov 15, 2026, before any of its code was written or run"
git_dirty_source_means: a file under src/ or a Python file in app/ differed from git_commit
what: Gradient boosting against the frozen forest and the 'D1 or worse now' rule on the 6-month outlook. Cost = 3 x missed + false alarms; lower is better, so a difference below zero favours boosting. The forest stays the reported system.

model.threshold_note: the fixed break-even threshold; not chosen on any data

comparisons.name: 6-month cost: boosting minus the frozen forest
comparisons.rows_used: the Rio Grande rows of the frozen outlook file (issued monthly, 2008 to 2025, full 52-week future known)
comparisons.year_unit: the calendar year of the issue date (the date the forecast was made), all counties together

block1.caveat: Percentile interval from 18 resampled years (block 1). With this few years it is too narrow: in simulation a nominal 95% interval covered the truth about 88% of the time with 8 years and 92% with 18 (80% and 90% with two-year blocks), and is expected to be less if years are dependent. These coverage figures come from a simulation with independent years and a true difference of zero, not from this project's data.

block2.caveat: Percentile interval from 18 resampled years (block 2). With this few years it is too narrow: in simulation a nominal 95% interval covered the truth about 88% of the time with 8 years and 92% with 18 (80% and 90% with two-year blocks), and is expected to be less if years are dependent. These coverage figures come from a simulation with independent years and a true difference of zero, not from this project's data.
